profiles.name: Ra / The Law of One
profiles.channeler: Carla L. Rueckert; Don Elkins as questioner; James (Jim) McCarty as scribe/support
profiles.classification: Claimed collective consciousness / social memory complex
profiles.origin: In the material, Ra identifies with a sixth-density collective associated with Venus.
profiles.dateBasis: Date of first numbered Ra session, retained by L/L Research.
profiles.summary: A 106-session question-and-answer corpus recorded from January 1981 through March 1984. L/L Research publishes session transcripts and recordings.
themes: Service to others and service to self
claims: The speaker is presented as a collective intelligence rather than a human personality.
The corpus offers a spiritual cosmology and a claimed account of ancient contact.
caveats: The record establishes a corpus and its reported production history, not an independently verified extraterrestrial source.
Ra's claimed ancient activity belongs in a belief chronology, separate from the modern documentary timeline.

profiles.name: Q'uo
profiles.channeler: Carla L. Rueckert and subsequent L/L Research channels
profiles.origin: L/L describes Q'uo as a collaboration involving Hatonn, Latwii and Ra.
profiles.dateBasis: First appearance identified by L/L's official timeline and matching session record.
profiles.summary: A continuing conscious-channeling tradition within L/L Research. Its archival relationship to Ra is explicit, while its claimed nonhuman collaboration remains a religious claim.
claims: The entity label represents a cooperative principle rather than one biological species.
caveats: Do not count Q'uo as an independently corroborating witness for Ra: both belong to the same institutional channeling tradition.
Conscious Q'uo sessions and the earlier Ra trance sessions are distinct bodies of material.

profiles.name: Hatonn in the L/L lineage
profiles.channeler: Walt Rogers in L/L's retrospective account; later Carla Rueckert and other L/L channels
profiles.origin: Described in L/L's narrative as a Confederation source; not a verified astronomical civilization.
profiles.dateBasis: L/L's retrospective account places Don Elkins's group experiment in 1962, drawing on Rogers's material.
profiles.summary: Hatonn is part of the pre-Ra history of L/L Research and later appears within Q'uo's reported composition.
claims: L/L's account describes telepathic contact with a group consciousness.
caveats: 1962 dates the L/L experiment, not the earliest possible appearance of the Hatonn name.
Do not merge unrelated later Hatonn-attributed publications solely because the name matches.

profiles.name: Ashtar / George W. Van Tassel
profiles.origin: The 1952 text situates Ashtar at patrol station Schare; later channels expand and vary the story.
profiles.dateBasis: Date heading of the Ashtar message in Van Tassel's published text.
profiles.summary: An early textual anchor for Ashtar narratives, preceding the Ra sessions by almost three decades.
claims: Van Tassel attributes the warning message to Ashtar.
caveats: A dated printed claim does not establish ET communication.
Later Ashtar or Ashtar Sheran channels are separate claimants; shared naming alone does not demonstrate common origin.

profiles.name: Seth / Jane Roberts
profiles.channeler: Jane Roberts; Robert F. Butts as recorder
profiles.origin: Presented as a nonphysical personality; not inherently an ET species claim.
profiles.dateBasis: Session 4 date; retrospective session notes distinguish Seth from the initial Frank Watts communication.
profiles.summary: A large body of recorded sessions and books associated with Roberts. The first numbered early session is dated December 2, 1963; the explicit Seth transition is placed in session 4.
claims: Roberts presented the material as communication from Seth.
caveats: Session date, later book publication and digitization dates must be kept separate.
The existence of recorded sessions and books does not verify the claimed nonphysical speaker.

profiles.name: Alice A. Bailey / Djwhal Khul
profiles.origin: Lucis Trust presents this as telepathic work with a Tibetan teacher, rather than an ET-species claim.
profiles.dateBasis: Month of contact reported in Lucis Trust's institutional history.
profiles.summary: An earlier example of books attributed to a nonordinary teacher. The related publishing organization was established in 1922.
claims: The texts are attributed within the tradition to telepathic collaboration.
caveats: 1919 is a reported contact onset; 1922 is an organizational/publication milestone.
The claimed teacher's identity is not established by the organizational history.

findings: Use Ra as the central research anchor, but include an earlier-history view: Spiritualism, Theosophy, Bailey, Ashtar and Seth predate the 1981 Ra sessions.
Keep a documentary timeline separate from claimed cosmic antiquity. Ancient-Egypt or Venus narratives are assertions inside texts, not independently dated historical events.

Entity labels are heterogeneous: Ashtar is a commander, Ra a collective, Q'uo a collaborative principle, Seth a nonphysical teacher and Djwhal Khul an esoteric master. A universal species list would misrepresent them.
Two different Ashtar channels are two attestations to a shared name, not independent verification of one entity.
Q'uo's relationship with Ra, Latwii and Hatonn is explicit in L/L's own account, so it should be mapped as an internal claimed relationship, not independent corroboration.
Official L/L full-page retrieval returned 403; findings are grounded in the search-indexed official records. Preserve this access limitation and do not imply a fresh complete audit of the archive.
Small chronology correction: the first Roberts–Butts numbered session (December 2, 1963) begins with Frank Watts; corpus notes place Seth's explicit replacement in session 4 (December 8).
